title: Modes: hear them in real music, then break them
what: A new Vamp lab section plays each mode's signature chords (Dorian's Dm to G, Mixolydian's D to C) and the characteristic note over them. Press Spoil it to add a V to I cadence and hear exactly which note ruins the mode. The timeline is now zoomable and filterable, there are real songs to listen for, and the exit ticket has three new questions.

title: Blueprint Drafting talks to real CAD and to Workbench
what: Download a drawing as a DXF for CAD software or a laser cutter, or import a DXF to trace. Build it in Workbench turns matching top, front and side views into a 3D model. If the views disagree, it identifies the size to fix.

title: Bridge Over Troubled Water opens on the build lab
what: The bridge lab now opens first and keeps tools beside the bridge on a sideways phone. Tests report which members carried load and which triangles helped. A maximum member length prevents one-beam shortcuts, and results stay consistent across devices and speed settings.

title: Omar Khayyam: the mathematician behind the Rubáiyát
what: A new pioneer lesson on Omar Khayyam: solve a cubic equation with a parabola and a circle the way he did, race his Jalali calendar against ours, bend Euclid's parallel postulate, then read the Rubáiyát in three layers (the Persian word for word, FitzGerald's 1859 and 1889 versions, with every change marked) and write your own AABA quatrain.

title: The Unit Factory is now a point-and-click factory floor
what: Explore a point-and-click factory: pull the lever, choose materials and planets, and follow Gauge’s guidance. Conversions show cancelling units and a balance. Turn 10 kg into a cube of different materials or a spring-scale reading on another world, then complete six work orders.

title: Live Sound Reinforcement: beat feedback and run the PA
what: A new live-sound lesson covers what happens after the mixer: decibels and the inverse square law, gain before feedback, ringing out a PA with a 31-band EQ (with sound and an ear-training mode), loudspeakers and beaming, amplifier loads and speaker cable, timing delay speakers, hunting hum and protecting your hearing, and the show-day order from load-in to debrief.

title: Path Studio is now a real vector editor: pen curves, editable points, Unite / Minus / Intersect
what: Draw curves with the Pen, edit anchors and handles, and add or delete points. Select, resize, rotate, group, align and space objects. Combine shapes with Unite, Minus front, Intersect or Exclude. Rectangles gain rounded corners, polygons can become stars, and text gets font choices.

title: The Recording Session: run a studio console, cues, patchbay and print
what: Run a recording session through channel and monitor paths, cue and FX sends, HearBack, patchbay normals, solo modes and mix printing. Learn why sessions use 24-bit / 48 kHz. Related lessons add EQ and compression comparisons, stereo microphone techniques and a 3:1 rule calculator.

title: Instrument lessons: play your first tune in one minute, at any age
what: Piano, guitar, violin, saxophone and drums now open with a playable instrument and a glowing first tune, so you can make music before reading a word. Tell it how much you have played and it gives you a short route. Lessons also add "In plain words" boxes you can have read aloud, and tips for children, teens and adults.

title: Sacred Measurements & Numbers
what: Measure Noah's Ark, the Ark of the Covenant, the Tabernacle and Solomon's Temple with a live cubit converter, to-scale plans, a numbers lab and a gematria tool.

title: Fake Book: Listen to me play, and take the band home as a MIDI file
what: Fake Book can listen through your microphone as you play. Note heads show pitch accuracy, and the session ends with a score and personal best. Any octave counts. Download the melody, chords, bass and drums as MIDI for GarageBand, MuseScore or BandLab.

title: 3D Design: this quarter's Trio Challenge
what: This quarter’s Trio Challenge asks for moving parts that stay together when printed, a useful tool and a likeness. Combine them in one print or spread them across several. The planner tracks each trait and its evidence. Slicer guidance covers hinges, joints and other moving parts.

title: Instrument lessons: a take-home page for every player
what: Print a one-page guide for piano, guitar, violin, saxophone or drums. Choose a child, young adult or adult version. Each sheet covers the first lesson, instrument care, goals from beginner to advanced, a 15-minute practice routine and a QR code back to the lesson.

title: Fake Book: choose your own guitar fingerings
what: Choose melody, melody + bass or chord-melody tab. Move through hand positions, shift octaves, or choose fingerings for individual beats. Nearby notes adapt to your choices, and your fingerings follow the song into a new key.

title: Egyptian Hieroglyphs: from royal cartouches to the Rosetta Stone
what: Use all 24 one-consonant signs, read royal cartouches and save your own. Compare Champollion’s Ptolemaios–Kleopatra inscriptions, solve determinative cases and test Eye of Horus fractions. Museum photos open in the lightbox.

title: Drum Lab: a Funky Rhythm Ladder you can print
what: Work through 68 numbered funk exercises while your hands keep a steady pattern. Each rung changes one feature, such as bass drum placement, ghost notes or hi-hat technique. Exercises play four times after a count-in and print as one-page handouts with tempo boxes.

title: Cymatics: a real Chladni plate
what: The plate simulator now solves the real plate equation: choose steel, aluminium, brass, glass or acrylic, set the size and thickness, drive it with a wave driver or a violin bow, and watch sand hop only where the plate beats gravity. Repeat Faraday's vacuum experiment with fine powder, read the real frequency, displacement and g-force, and work through seven experiments.

title: Seeing Light Lab, rebuilt with real science
what: Follow light from a lamp to a ball to your eye, watch a pupil change size at its real width from starlight to sunshine, see the upside-down picture on your retina, and watch colors fade to gray as your rods take over in the dark. Plus hands-on tests and public-domain photos from NASA, Gray's Anatomy and Ibn al-Haytham's Book of Optics.

title: Revelation, retold in nine acts
what: Revelation is now a full illuminated lesson: the whole story retold act by act from Patmos to the New Jerusalem, the seven cities and their history, a Roman coin with seven stars, the papyrus that reads 616, an echo finder for its Old Testament images, the sevens explained, and four ways Christians have read it.

title: Ezekiel: the whole story, and where it leads
what: Read Ezekiel as a story in three acts, from the throne-chariot by the canal to the river that heals the Dead Sea, then follow eight threads from Ezekiel to Jesus, the Spirit and Revelation's new creation.

title: Drop Voicings: Open Up the Chord
what: Stack a seventh chord, count voices from the top and drop one an octave. Hear Drop 2, Drop 3 and Drop 2 & 4, see them on a staff, keyboard and guitar fretboard, find the smoothest path through a ii–V–I, then build voicings yourself.

title: Running the Allen & Heath Qu-7
what: Practise gain, 48V phantom power, monitor mixes with Sends on Faders, and scenes on the class Qu-7, with a lab for each.

title: Roguelike Builder: Make Your Own Rogue
what: Build a dungeon crawler where one word builds a whole dungeon, check it with flood fill, balance the fights with dice math, and then walk the same dungeon in 3D in our Crawlspace showcase game.

title: Text Adventure Builder: Make Your Own Zork
what: Type your way through a haunted school, a space station or Paul's shipwreck on Malta, build the whole text-adventure engine yourself, and use breadth-first search to prove your own map can be solved.

title: Lemonade Tycoon Builder: Make Your Own Business Game
what: Run a lemonade stand, find the best price with a little arithmetic, and build the whole economy game yourself. Then turn it into a school store, a food truck or a 3D-print farm.

title: Trail Game Builder: Make Your Own Oregon Trail
what: Build a survival-on-the-road game from scratch, play with a Trail Lab you can reconfigure, and design a spin-off: Mars, the Silk Road, the deep sea, or your own idea.

title: Wireless Mics & RF Coordination
what: Place up to 8 wireless mics in the UHF band, see why intermodulation collides with carriers, and dodge TV stations.

title: 3D printing: the Fold & Unfold blueprint game
what: A CAD-style drafting studio with a ribbon, command line and blueprint sheet. In Unfold you draw a 3D part's top, front and right views. In Fold you read a blueprint and stack blocks on the print bed until your part matches. Hard mode adds dashed hidden lines, and a glass box unfolds to show where each view comes from.

title: Fake Book: pick your instrument and practise step by step
what: Choose what you play (trumpet, sax, guitar, voice and more) and the music changes to fit your instrument. Five practice buttons take you from listening to trading fours. You can also search for tunes, get a random one with Surprise me, drag across measures to loop them, and use the speed trainer, which raises the tempo a little each time the loop comes round.

title: Beethoven: the Moonlight Sonata and the Fifth, complete
what: Read and play the whole “Moonlight” Sonata, all three movements, and the complete first movement of the Fifth Symphony for full orchestra. Each score has a bar-by-bar guide that follows the music, and the section labels on every composer score are readable again.

title: Beethoven: what he worked with
what: Drag a year slider from 1796 to 1827 to hear how Beethoven's hearing changed and see how he adapted at each stage, meet percussionist Evelyn Glennie, try a bone-conduction experiment, watch an orchestra play the Fifth, compare Mozart and Beethoven side by side, and sort Beethoven myths from facts.

title: The Violin: now a full lesson
what: Learn the parts of the violin and bow, how to hold both, how to tighten and rosin the bow, check the bridge and tune by ear (with a tuning game), then explore the fingerboard to think in fifths.

title: The Saxophone: a history timeline
what: Follow the saxophone from Adolphe Sax's 1846 patent to Coleman Hawkins, Charlie Parker and John Coltrane on a zoomable timeline with photos. Press Play the story for a guided tour.

title: Tinkercad Codeblocks: a star fidget that stays together
what: New Locked fidget layout in the Ring Stack Lab: rings with a ridge that sits in the next ring's groove, so lifting the outer ring brings the whole fidget with it. Try the lift test, see a falls-apart warning when the lock fails, and download a print-in-place STL. Includes the Codeblocks recipe (slab and ring templates) for a star or round fidget.

title: Seeing Breath in Wi-Fi
what: Now readable on a phone: the claims table turns into cards. New jump bar, a claims worksheet that saves your answers, and a predict-first step before the Room lab.

title: Walt Disney: the Flywheel strategy map
what: A new interactive map shows how Disney's film studio, TV, music, books, merchandise and theme park all fed each other. Press any box to see what it gives and gets, or walk one trip around the loop.

title: Pick your guitar shapes
what: Choose guitar chord shapes with finger numbers, barres and roots marked. Hear each shape and use your selection in sheet diagrams, bar pop-ups and playback. Choices are saved for each tune.

title: Character modeling: a real humanoid base mesh
what: The character creator now starts from a proper humanoid template: one smooth body with a ribcage, shoulders, glutes, knees, calves and a shaped face, in an A-pose. Pick Explorer, Scholar, Guardian, Mystic, Inventor or Athlete, then change proportions, face, hair and outfit. It exports as one solid body that is ready to print.

title: 3D Design: build anything in Workbench
what: Workbench brings 3D building to the browser. Add shapes, cut holes, group and repeat parts, and animate them on a timeline. Start with a house, fidget spinner, phone stand or treasure chest. Export STL for printing or animated GLB for a game.

title: Deuteronomy: six lenses, hard questions, and a depth dial
what: Moses’ farewell speeches now unfold through six lenses (memory, the Shema, justice, limits on power, remembering, choosing life) that each link to the passage, forward into later Scripture, and to a hard question. Pick Guided, Build, or Investigate depth, test yourself with seven questions, and write a four-part reflection that saves in your browser.

title: Theatre Cue Sheets: a worked example from The Pirates of Penzance
what: See a stage manager's marked script for the opening of The Pirates of Penzance, the cue sheet it turns into, and the exact words called on headset. Plus prompt books from 1720 and 1861 and the lighting boards that answer GO.

title: Stage Plotting: from a libretto to a ground plan
what: Decode W. S. Gilbert's set description for The Pirates of Penzance (“Rock L. sloping down to L.C.”) into a measured ground plan with an item list you can enter in the designer. Plus photos of real stages, a fly rail, and an 1876 theatre plan.

title: Jim Henson: Camera Frame Lab
what: Be the camera operator on a puppet set: move the camera, tilt and lens until the puppet is framed and the puppeteer is hidden, then race to steer a puppet using only the monitor, which isn't a mirror. Plus an archival photo gallery.

title: Walt Disney: Animation Lab
what: Try animating a bouncing ball on ones and on twos, see why slow-in and squash & stretch make it feel real, and fly a multiplane camera through a painted scene to see parallax. Plus an archival photo gallery and the engineers behind Disney's inventions.

title: Jesus’ Ministry: eight scenes and the big question
what: The Jesus’ Ministry lesson now has a scene board that walks through eight moments from the baptism to Caesarea Philippi, a place-and-art gallery, a map, a new investigation on the paralyzed man (Mark 2), fuller notes on each lens, and nine passages to read.

title: Weather Watch: live storm desk
what: See rain arrive minute by minute, track warned storms and lightning on a map you can drag, read the storm outlook, follow hurricanes, replay Charley, Irma and Ian, and click anywhere to analyze it. A Practice storm works on clear days.

title: Feasts: from Leviticus 23 to the table
what: The Feasts of Israel lesson now has a Leviticus scroll fragment, a Seder plate, a shofar, and a painting of Yom Kippur prayer, new notes on Trumpets, Atonement, and Nehemiah's revival of Booths, and nine passages to read.

title: Joshua to David: evidence and art
what: The Joshua to David lesson now has a tribal-allotments map, paintings of Samson, Ruth, and David, photos of Jericho and Khirbet Qeiyafa, the Tel Dan inscription, a new investigation on Judges 21:25, and nine passages to read.

title: Psalms: explore all 150
what: The Psalms lesson is now a full study page like Proverbs: explore every psalm and verse in three translations, highlight psalms by kind, read notes on craft and context, annotate Psalm 13, and compare Psalm 88 with Psalm 150.

title: Holy Week: from Palm Sunday to the empty tomb
what: The Holy Week lesson now has six day-by-day lenses, paintings by Giotto, Leonardo, Doré, and Grünewald, photos of Gethsemane's olive trees, the Pilate Stone replica, the Caiaphas ossuary, and a tomb's rolling stone, plus nine passages to read, including Zechariah 9:9 and the washing of the disciples' feet.

title: Exodus: from Pharaoh to Sinai
what: The Exodus lesson now has a Sinai map, Egypt and wilderness photos, paintings of the burning bush, the plagues, the sea, and Moses, a modern Passover Seder plate, a new investigation on Exodus 20:2, and nine passages to read.

title: Genesis: art, Ur, and the promise
what: The Genesis lesson now has artists' pictures of creation, the fall, and Babel next to a photo of the ziggurat of Ur, a Joseph painting, a map of Abram's world, a new investigation on the blessing in Genesis 12:1–3, and nine passages to read.

title: Revelation: maps, cities, and artists
what: The Revelation lesson now has a seven-churches map, photos of Patmos, Ephesus, and Pergamon, Dürer and Angers artwork of the Four Horsemen, a Lion-and-Lamb investigation, and nine passages to read, including the letter to Laodicea and the river of life.

title: Violin in the chord views
what: The Piano | Guitar switch now has a Violin option in the live chord view, the Chords tab and the bar pop-up. A violin plays chord tones one at a time, so you see every tone of the chord, triad or scale on the first-position fingerboard with its finger number, and hear it as an arpeggio.

title: Finger positions under every measure
what: Instead of tab, turn on Finger positions to see a small fingerboard under each measure with the fingers placed on it for guitar or violin. The hand stays put from bar to bar when it can, and a dashed ring shows where the last bar ended so you can follow the hand along.

title: Play the melody on violin
what: The melody panel now has a Violin tab. For every note it shows the string, which finger to use (and whether it sits low or high on the fretless board), and which position your hand is in, with a sound check from the violin voice.

title: Print any score from the Fake Book
what: Press Print notation to get your song on letter paper: a title block, big clear staves, and page breaks that never cut a line of music in half. Songs you imported (MusicXML or iReal) have their own print button too.

title: Fake Book song map and zoom
what: Long songs get a song map in the play bar: click or drag to jump to any bar, zoom out, or press Fit song to see the whole piece at once.

title: Fake Book playback and bass staff
what: Click a bar, then press Play to start right there. A Click button turns the metronome and count-in off. Busy left-hand triplets now show as clean beamed groups.

title: Fake Book note names
what: Show colored letter names right on the notes in both treble and bass clef, or switch to names under the staff. Meter labels now show only where the meter changes, and fewer false key labels.

title: Volcano Simulator
what: Compare magma cutaways with crystal mush, event stages, true-scale controls, source-tagged evidence and separate reservoir, melt and erupted volumes.

title: Fake Book
what: Read melody, chords, bass clef, and guitar tab from MusicXML songs.

title: Chemistry expansion
what: Build atoms and test Dalton’s rules against modern evidence.

title: Archimedes’ Principle
what: Explore buoyancy with the new shared liquid engine.
